sections.bio:
I design and ship production AI systems. Not prototypes. Not demos. Systems that run at scale, serve real users, and generate measurable business outcomes.
 
As a Technical Founder, I have built and operate three active AI products:
 
SimplyAI  An AI Operations consultancy delivering enterprise workflow automation. I architect end-to-end LLM pipelines that replace manual operations, integrate with existing enterprise systems, and deploy to production with full monitoring.
 
SimplySites.gr and SimplyNewspaper A high-scale AI content distribution and SEO automation engine. Fully deterministic publishing pipelines with zero human editorial intervention, built on Next.js, Supabase, FastAPI, and OpenAI APIs.
 
Ampassador  A Multi-Agent Legal Intelligence and Negotiation Co-Pilot. Autonomous LLM agents handle contract analysis, clause extraction, legal risk identification, and AI-driven negotiation assistance. Built with LangGraph, FastAPI, RAG pipelines over legal corpora, and a full Next.js and TypeScript frontend.
 
My core stack: Python, FastAPI, Next.js, TypeScript, OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, LangChain, LangGraph, Pinecone, Chroma, PostgreSQL, Docker, Vercel.
 
I think in systems. I own outcomes end-to-end: architecture, implementation, deployment, and iteration.
 
Available for remote roles worldwide. Open to relocation to Barcelona or Cyprus.
 
If you are building something serious with AI, let's talk.
 
📧 [email protected]

I rebuilt the viral Carvana AI workflow for Greece.

Most people saw the viral "AI finds underpriced cars" video.

The problem?

It was built for the US.

Kelley Blue Book doesn't work in Greece.

Auto-messaging Facebook sellers is a fast way to get banned.

So I rebuilt the entire system from scratch.

Instead of copying the prompt...

...I built an AI workflow designed for the Greek market.

The system includes:

→ Car.gr + AutoTriti listing scanner

→ Greek market valuation engine (using local comps instead of KBB)

→ SQLite deal database that tracks every listing

→ AI deal scoring based on comparable listings

→ Telegram approval workflow (the AI drafts messages, you decide whether to send them)

→ Claude skills (/car-scan, /car-value, /car-outreach, /car-daily) that automate the entire pipeline

The goal isn't to let AI buy cars for you.

It's to spend your time evaluating the best opportunities instead of manually searching hundreds of listings.

I documented the complete architecture, prompts, database schema, and workflow so anyone can build it themselves.

But hiring a CFO costs $150K+ a year.

So most solopreneurs just... don't look.

A fractional CFO that reads your actual data, every Monday morning, in 2 minutes flat.

THE MONDAY MONEY REVIEW SYSTEM

The only missing piece is a prompt that knows what to do with them.

Here is what the full guide covers:

This is not theory.

One weekend. One setup. Runs every week after that.

Your landing page is leaking conversions.

Not because your copy is bad.

Not because your design is wrong.

Because you built it once and walked away.

The best SaaS founders treat their landing page like a living product.

It watches visitors.
It runs experiments.
It learns what works.
It proposes the next improvement.

Here is how to build one that does exactly that.

1. Ship the page first

You cannot optimize a page that does not exist.

Use Claude Code, Cursor, v0, Lovable, or Bolt to build a simple landing page:

Hero.
CTA.
Features.
Proof.
FAQ.
Footer.

One important detail:

give your main CTA button a stable name in the code.

Example:
primary-cta
data-cta="primary"

This makes it easy to track and test later.

2. Give it real analytics

A landing page without analytics is just guessing.

Add Microsoft Clarity or PostHog.

Clarity gives you free heatmaps and recordings.
PostHog gives you recordings, analytics, flags, and experiments in one tool.

Now you can see where people click, stop scrolling, rage-click, and disappear.

3. Run your first A/B test

Stop debating headlines in your head.

Let visitors vote.

Show half your visitors version A.
Show the other half version B.

Measure the action that matters:

signup
demo booked
purchase
CTA click

Use PostHog, GrowthBook, Statsig, Vercel Flags, or VWO.

One rule:

do not stop the test just because one version looks like it is winning early.

That is how founders fool themselves with fake signal.

4. Let AI propose the next test

This is where it gets interesting.

Once a week, an AI agent reads your experiment results.

It checks what won.
It checks what failed.
It proposes one next test.

Not ten.
One.

Example:

“Variant B improved CTA clicks by 18%. Next test: change the pricing headline.”

The agent can draft the variant, but it should not ship it live.

The agent proposes.
You approve.

Automate the analysis.
Keep the taste human.

5. Personalize the page by visitor behavior

A first-time visitor should not always see the same page as someone who visited pricing twice.

With PostHog cohorts, GrowthBook, or Vercel Flags, you can show different hero copy based on behavior.

Not IP address.

Actual behavior:

visited pricing
clicked CTA but did not convert
returned after 7 days
read multiple pages

That is when the page stops being static.

It becomes adaptive.

6. Create a weekly iteration ritual

Every Monday, 30 minutes.

Review the data.
Pick one hypothesis.
Schedule one test.
Log the result.

After a few months, you will have a conversion playbook specific to your audience.

Most founders never do this because it sounds complicated.

It is not.

It just requires consistency.

Your landing page should not be a poster.

It should be a feedback loop.

Comment “PAGE” and I’ll send you the setup for turning a static page into a self-improving system.

A $15,000 longevity coach just became optional.

Here is why

The top 1% used to pay for private access to protocols that took decades to develop. Blood panels, sleep optimization, VO2 max testing, supplement stacks, hormonal tracking.

Now AI can do most of that for free.

I have spent the last 6 months testing this. Here is what I found:


NEVER guess at your longevity protocol again.

7 things AI now does better than most $15K coaches:


1. Biomarker interpretation

Upload your bloodwork. Ask Claude or GPT to flag anything outside optimal longevity ranges (not just "normal" ranges). Most doctors optimize for sick, not for thriving. AI knows the difference.


2. Personalized supplement stacking

Describe your goals, your deficiencies, your medications. AI will cross-reference interactions, dosing windows, and peer-reviewed research in under 60 seconds. A human coach bills 3 hours for this.


3. Sleep architecture analysis

Connect your Oura or Whoop data. Paste your weekly report into Claude. Ask it to identify patterns suppressing your deep sleep or REM. It will give you 5 actionable fixes by morning.


4. Continuous glucose monitoring interpretation

CGM data is useless without context. AI turns your glucose spikes into a personalized food and timing roadmap. No nutritionist required.


5. Protocol design

Tell AI your age, goals, current habits, and budget. Ask it to build a 90-day longevity protocol prioritizing the highest ROI interventions. It will cite the studies. Your coach probably did not.


6. Accountability systems

AI helps you build habit stacks, design weekly check-ins with yourself, and create tracking frameworks. The accountability was always the most expensive part of coaching.


7. Research synthesis

A new longevity study drops. Paste the abstract. Ask AI how it applies to your current protocol. You are now running on information your coach will not read for another 6 months.


The real advantage wealthy people had was not the coach.

It was access to information, systems, and interpretation.

AI just democratized all three.


The caveat: AI does not replace a physician. Get labs done. Work with doctors for clinical decisions. Use AI to come prepared, ask better questions, and go deeper between appointments.


I put together a full starter prompt library for longevity optimization. 12 prompts you can use today across sleep, nutrition, fitness, and biomarkers.

Comment "LONGEVITY" and I'll send it to you.
